item.text:
The HVAC demand flexibility measures are **upgrades 24–28**, as confirmed by the [official ResStock 2025 Release 1 upgrade list](https://resstock.nlr.gov/datasets). They differ in **when** the thermostat changes, **how long** the change lasts, and **the temperature offset**.

| Upgrade | Measure | Thermostat action |
|---|---|---|
| **24** | On-peak load shedding, **2°F offset** | During a **4-hour peak period**, lower the heating setpoint or raise the cooling setpoint by 2°F. |
| **25** | **4-hour pre-peak** load shifting, **2°F offset** | Preheat by raising the heating setpoint, or precool by lowering the cooling setpoint, by 2°F for 4 hours before peak. |
| **26** | On-peak load shedding, **4°F offset** | Same timing as 24, with a larger 4°F adjustment. |
| **27** | **4-hour pre-peak** load shifting, **4°F offset** | Same timing as 25, with a larger 4°F preconditioning adjustment. |
| **28** | **1-hour pre-peak** load shifting, **2°F offset** | Same temperature adjustment as 25, with a shorter, 1-hour preconditioning period. |

**Shedding** reduces HVAC demand by relaxing temperature settings during peak hours. **Shifting** moves heating or cooling earlier, using the building’s stored warmth or coolness to reduce subsequent demand; settings return to baseline during peak hours. The final release treats these as separate strategies, without combining them. See [HVAC Load Flexibility measure documentation, §4.4, Table 8](https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/93846.pdf).

I started at your [release index](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NatLabRockies/buildstock-corpus/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1-v1/processed/resstock/resstock_amy2018_2025_release_1/index.json), but its JSON contents did not render in the browsing tool; the identification and comparison above use the official sources linked here.
